column1: # Answers whose order v4 itself does not fix. Two v4 processes on the same
# database give them in different orders (parity/run.sh --test v4-twin), so
# no fixed order in irrd-ng can match v4 byte for byte. For these, and only
# these, whois_diff.py also accepts an answer that is a permutation of v4's,
# reports it as "equivalent" with the divergence id, never as "identical",
# and --strict turns it back into a difference. Everything else is compared
# byte for byte. An entry here needs the v4 code reference and a twin run
# that shows the nondeterminism; it is reviewed like a divergence.
# mode<TAB>query regex (v4's view of the query)<TAB>answer regex or -<TAB>divergence<TAB>why
# (mode header: the third column is a header name; for http heads, the
#  query regex matches "METHOD PATH" of corpus/http/requests.tsv items)
# tokens: the framing line (A<len>) must match exactly; the payload must hold
#   the same tokens (split on whitespace and commas) in any order.
# objects: the answer must hold the same objects, with the same sequence
#   of v4 sort keys (rpsl_pk: first attribute, nic-hdl for person/role,
#   prefix+origin for route/route6; ip_first and asn_first follow from it);
#   only objects whose keys are equal may come in a different order.
tokens
